sections.h2: Where is Toombs County, and which towns are in it?
sections.html:
Toombs County is in southeast Georgia, with Lyons holding the courthouse and Vidalia ranking as the biggest city. State lawmakers established it on August 18, 1905, as Georgia's 144th county and it organized that October, per Wikipedia.

Land came from Tattnall and Montgomery counties, and a sliver of Emanuel County joined in 1907 to complete today's outline. Total area is 371 square miles. Streams south of Vidalia reach the Altamaha, while those in the Lyons half of the county run to the Ohoopee.

The cities are Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia, with Ohoopee counted by the Census Bureau as a place of its own. Center, English Eddy, Normantown and South Thompson have no municipal government. Emanuel, Candler, Tattnall, Appling, Jeff Davis, Montgomery and Treutlen counties touch its borders. The county sits within the Vidalia micropolitan area, and the Toombs County School District runs its public schools.

sections.h2: How affordable are Toombs County homes?
sections.html:
Of the four counties covered together here, Toombs has the least expensive houses. The 2020-2024 median is $137,000, and owners occupy 60.5% of units.

Toombs County housing and income figures from Census QuickFacts (units and permits are 2025 data; the rest cover 2020-2024)

The county recorded just 35 building permits for 2025, so nearly every sale involves an existing house. The 2020 census tallied 10,505 households among 12,027 housing units, 12.7% of them empty, with 9.5% of rentals vacant. Population is estimated at 27,545 for mid-2025, up 1.9% from the 2020 base. Poverty stands at 22.8%, the highest of the four, and 16.3% of those under 65 lack health insurance.

sections.h2: Which office mails the bill, and which sets the value?
sections.html:
The commissioner handles billing and collection from 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, Lyons, GA 30436. The phone is (912) 526-8575. Weekday service runs from half past eight to half past four.

The county tax site's FAQ gives (912) 526-6291 for the assessors, who determine value and take returns and exemption forms. For a copy of your warranty deed, go to the clerk of superior court's deed room in the courthouse.

  • Tax commissioner: statements, payments, decals for mobile homes, delinquent sales
  • Assessors: valuation, returns, homestead filings, first-level appeals
  • Equalization board: named by the Grand Jury to hear disputes
  • County commissioners and school board: adopt the millage rates

The commissioner does not decide value or rates, the county site stresses. Anyone upset about how large the bill is should talk to the elected boards that levy it.

sections.h2: What is the Toombs County due date, and what happens after it?
sections.html:
The county's pages contradict each other. The information page has statements leaving the office by October 20 and payment owed on December 20. The FAQ has been naming November 15 for real estate and business personal property since 2018.

Rely on the date on your own statement and call (912) 526-8575 if it looks off. The FAQ adds interest of 1% monthly after the deadline and a 10% penalty on tax unpaid 90 days out. Past 30 days, a fi. fa., which is a recorded lien, may be filed. Those records are open to the public, so credit bureaus can see them.

  • Interest on real estate: 1% each month
  • Penalty once 90 days pass: 10%
  • Lien: allowed once 30 days pass unpaid
  • Mobile homes: April 1, then 10% plus 1% a month

An auction on the courthouse steps was announced for December 2, 2025, at 10 a.m. That date has gone by. The list for any sale can be seen at the office, where staff can tell you the next one.

sections.h2: What should a Toombs County seller do about unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Before you sign a contract, have the commissioner state the parcel's balance in writing. Georgia's revenue department says no refund exists for a part year, which leaves the January 1 owner holding the whole amount.

Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia are cities, and a home inside one may owe city tax along with county tax. Ask whether both apply. If you have fallen behind, check the clerk's records for a recorded lien too, since a title company will want it released. When the roof, wiring or plumbing needs money you lack, an as-is cash buyer removes the repair bill, and any tax owed comes out of the price at closing.

A clear payoff letter and a copy of the recorded deed are the two papers that move a closing fastest.

sections.h2: Must a Toombs County owner file a property return?
sections.html:
Anything taxable that you own on January 1 is supposed to be returned to the assessors during the first three months of the year, ending April 1, according to the county information page. An owner who files nothing is treated as repeating last year's final value and real estate exemptions.

An owner who thinks the value is too high may file a return giving their own opinion of market value, and the information page says that filing establishes appeal rights if the assessors change the figure again. The FAQ lists real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber among the taxes the commissioner bills.

  • Window: opens January 1, closes April 1
  • Silence: last year's value and exemptions repeat
  • Own-value return: sets up an appeal if the assessors disagree

Household goods are not normally taxable, per the same FAQ, so a seller does not owe tax on furniture left in the house.

sections.h2: Which homestead amounts appear on the Toombs County site?
sections.html:
The county's information page prints the regular exemption for owners who live in the house before January 1. As printed, the amounts are $20,000 off assessed value for county operations, $2,000 off county school tax and $2,000 off the state share. A city house gets a further $10,000 off city and city school tax.

Further categories carry labels: S3 for age 62 and up with an income test, S4 and SC for age 65 and up, S5 for disabled veterans, SS for unremarried surviving spouses, and a local school-tax exemption at 70 and over. The 62-and-over school exemption uses a $10,000 earned-income limit for the prior year. Because details vary by category, ask the assessors which one fits your situation.

Applications are received between January 1 and April 1, and the page notes that state law allows no extension. Once approved, the exemption repeats yearly until eligibility changes. Moving to a new address means filing again.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Toombs County assessment?
sections.html:
Mail a letter to the Toombs County assessors. The 45 days are counted from the date on the notice, and the county site says notices tend to arrive in spring.

Valid grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. Three tracks are open: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. A dispute can then move on to Superior Court. Mobile homes keep a separate clock. A different value may be declared inside 45 days of the bill mailing, the county says, and a change notice opens a 21-day window to go to the equalization board.

faqs.q: What is the best way to reach the Toombs County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Phone (912) 526-8575 or visit 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, in Lyons, any weekday between half past eight and half past four.

faqs.q: Does Toombs County tax come due in November or December?
faqs.a: The county's pages disagree, with December 20 on one and November 15 on the FAQ. Use the date on your bill, and double-check with the commissioner.

faqs.q: What does paying Toombs County tax late cost?
faqs.a: One percent interest accrues monthly after the deadline, and tax still open 90 days later takes a 10% penalty. A lien may be filed after 30 days.

faqs.q: When are Toombs County mobile home taxes due?
faqs.a: They fall due each April 1. Later payments draw a 10% filing penalty plus 1% per month, and a location permit and decal come only after full payment.

faqs.q: How much time does an owner get to dispute a Toombs County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, starting at the date on the assessment notice. Write to the assessors and say which route you want: equalization board, hearing officer or arbitrator.
